lS:2979-1964

Indian Standard SPECIFICATION FOR -FUSEL OIL
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 13 October 1964, after the draft finalized by the Alcohols and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Fuse1 oil is a by-product of the alcoholic fermentation of starches and sugars, and is obtained during the redistillation of crude ethyl alcohol. The percentage of fuse1 oil recovered varies from 0.05 to 0.2 percent on the quantity of ethyl alcohol manufactured. 0.2.i Fuse1 oil consists of higher primary alcohols, principally amyl and butyl, in their various isomeric forms. Traces of aldehydes, esters, alkaloids, etc, have also been reported. The composition of the material varies according to the source. Both crude and refined fuse1 oils are available, although the refined variety is the one used commercially. 0.2.2 Amongst its various uses, it is an excellent lacquer solvent specially due to its unusual blending properties which impart flow and gloss to the lacquers. It is extensively used in protective coiting formulations. It is also used as an industrial solvent, alone or in combination. It is also used in the manufacture of amyl acetate and other amyl compounds, pharmaceuticals, flavours, xanthates, etc. Through fractipnation of fuse1 oil as such or after esterification, amyl and butyl alcohols or their esters, both of which are excellent solvents, can also be obtained. 0.3 Realizing the versatility of this material, `the Alcohols and Allied Products Sectional Committee, considered it imperative to formulate a standard specification on the material, in order to make available to all concerned the minimum quality requirements of the material, through the medium of a national standard on the subject. 0.4 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on alcohols and allied products. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard iS complied with, the final-value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or Analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 3.

The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : 2 - 1960*. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1, SCOPE

'

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for fuse1 oil which is used as a thinner and solvent for protective coating formulations and for the manufacture of amyl alcohol.
2. REQmEMENTS

2.1 Description

-The material shall consist essentially of primary higher alcohols, principally amyl and butyl, in their various isomeric forms. It shall be homogeneous, clear, free from sediment and suspended matter.
2.2 The material shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1.

3, PACKING AND MARKING 3.1 Packing 3.1.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the material shall be packed in galvanized drums ( conforming to IS : 2552- 1963* ) or in any other containers subject to the provisions of law in force in the country for the time being.
3.1.2 All containers in which the material is packed shall be dry and clean so that no impurities harmful to the end use of the material are introduced. 3.2 Marking

3.2.1 The material shall be supplied in accordance and delivery instructions given by the purchaser.
3.2.2 Each container shall be marked with: a) Name of the material; b) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark, c) Tare, gross and net weight; and d) Lot and batch number.
I

with the marking

if any;

3.2.3 Each container shall have the caution label `FLAMMABLE' together with the corresponding symbol for labelling of dangerous goods (see Fig. 3 of IS : 1260- 1958t). It shall be further subject to the provisions of law in force at that time.
NOTE 1 -Necessary safeguards against the risk arising from the storage and handling of large volumes of flammable liquids shall be provided and all due precautions shall be taken ,at all times to prevent accidents by fire or explosion. when they are opened for the purpose of cleaning and rendering NOTE 2 -Except them free from fuse1 oil vapour, all empty tanks or other containers shall be kept securely closed unless they have been cleaned and freed from fuse1 oil vapour.

3.2*4 The containers may also be marked suitably with the IS1 Certification Mark. NOTE- The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act, and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under `which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

APPENDIX [ `Tuble 1, Item
DETERMINATION A-O. GENERAL

A
(iii) ] CONTENT

dF ETHANOL

A-O.1 Outline of MethodEstimation of ethanol contained in fuse1 oil presents difficulties because higher alcohols are also volatile along with ethanol and steam. Removal of higher alcohols from ethanol before distillation is therefore essential. Higher alcohols which are comparatively ins'oluble in brine are dissolved in petroleum hydrocarbon solvent and are removed leaving ethanol dissolved in brine and free from higher alcohols. Ethanol is subsequently distilled off from brine and its content determined by the pyknometric method. A-l. REAGENTS A-l.1 Petroleum IS : 1745- 196lt. Hydrocarbon Solvent 60/80-conforming to

*Specificationfor water, distilledquality ( revised ).
+Specification for petroleum hydrocarbon solvents.

6

IS t 2979- 1964 A-l.2 Saturated Brine Solution in water. A-2. PROCEDURE A-2.1 Shake 50 ml of the material vigorously for 5 minutes in a separator with 25 ml of petroleum hydrocarbon solvent and 100 ml of saturated After standing for 15 minutes the lower layer is drawn off brine solution. into a second separator and extracted with 50 ml of petroleum hydrocarbon solvent. The lower layer is drawn off into a distillation flask. Meanwhile, the fuse1 oil in the first separator is shaken with two successive quantities of 25 ml of saturated brine solution which after being extracted with petroleum hydrocarbon solvent in the second separator, are added to the liquid in the distillation flask and distilled. Collect 95 ml of the distillate in a lOO-ml measuring flask, made up to the mark with water at room temperature and determine the percentage ethanol by the pyknometric method. B-0.1 Outline of MethodConcentrated sulphuric acid renders normal constituents of fuse1 oil soluble which dissolve leaving any mineral oil present and which is detected by the resulting solution being transparent or not. / / B-l. PROCEDURE B-l.1 Mix 1 ml of the material and 1 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid (conforming to IS : 266 - 1961* ) in a test tube and cool. Add 1 ml of water and mix thoroughly. B-l.2 The material shall be regarded to have passed the test if the liquid thus obtained remains transparent. *Specificationfor sulphuricacid ( revised). 7

D-2. SAMPLING D-2.0 The following

INSTRUMENTS forms of sampling instruments may be used: from various depths

a) Weighted sampling in large tanks, and b) Sampling tube.

can for taking

samples

D-2.1 Weighted Sampling Can-of suitable capacity, 500 to 1000 *ml, and of such a weight as to sink readily in the material to be sampled. It is provided with a means to permit filling at any desired level and has an attached long chain or cord for the purpose (see Fig. 1 ). The metal used to weight the apparatus shall be fitted` externally, as irregularities in the metal are likely to contaminate the sample if the weight is fitted internally. 9

Is:2!#79-1964

FIG. 1 WEIGHTED SAXPLINQ CAN

D-2.2 Sampling Tube - It is made of metal or thick glass and is 20 to 40 mm in diameter and 400 to 600 mm in length ( see Fig. 2 ). The upper and lower ends are conical and reach 5 to 10 mm diameter at the narrow ends. Handling is facilitated by two rings at the upper end. For taking a sample, the apparatus is first closed at the top with the thumb or a It is then opened stopper and lowered until the desired depth is reached. for a short time to admit the material and finally closed and withdrawn. D-3. SCALE

OF SAMPLING

D-3.1 Lot - In any consignment all the containers of the same size and drawn from the same batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is known to consist of different batches of manufacture or of different sizes of containers, the containers belonging to the same batch and size shall be grouped together and each such group shall constitute a separate lot. D-3.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the material in a lot to the requirements of this specification, tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. For this purpose 5 containers shall be selected at random from each lot. `11

`IS : 2979 - 1964 D-3.2.1 In the case of very small lots where the selection of 5 containers may be uneconomical, the number of containers to be selected and the method of judging the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the specification shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
D-3.3 The containers shall be selected ness of selection the following procedure

/

at random and to ensure randomis recommended for use:

Starting from any container in the lot, count them as I, 2, . . . . up to r and so on in one order, where Y is the integral part of .N/5 ( .N being the number of containers in the lot ). Every rth container thus counted shall be withdrawn to constitute a sample till the required number of 5 containers are obtained.

D-4. PREPARATION

OF TEST

SAMPLES

D-4.1 From each of the containers

selected according to D-3.3, a representative portion of the material sufficient for carrying out tests as prescribed in 3 shall be drawn with the help of a suitable instrument (see D-2). D-4.2 Out of these portions, equal quantity of material shall be taken and mixed thoroughly to form a composite sample of about 1000 ml. The composite test sample shall be divided into 3 equal parts, one for the purchaser, another for the supplier and the third to be used as a referee sample. D-4.3 The composite samples shall be transferred to separate containers and shall be sealed and marked with full identification particulars given in D-1.7. D-4.4 The referee test sample shall also bear the seals of both the purchaser and the supplier. It shall be kept at a place agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, to be used in the case of any dispute between the two.
